It made a belly landing in a sugar beet field in Suffolk. Its recovery was featured in the June 1944 issue of Popular Science magazine. As a testament to the legendary toughness of the B-17, once it was jacked up onto its own landing gears, and some mobile repairs done to the engines and propellers, it was able to fly on its own back to a maintenance depot for more extensive repairs.[/p][p]Returned to duty the aircraft flew two more sorties. The aircraft attempted to limp home again but was forced to ditch into the North Sea[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/7d6ed1bea4fd244a553fc76c1a46f53897937ce9.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]This build is dedicated to the memory of John 'Lucky' Luckadoo, last B-17 pilot of the Bloody Hundredth, who passed away earlier this month.

Brave the deadly skies of occupied Europe![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/b9cf358297bbb4a2d98ef4aa459264f8b2430413.png"][/img]
[/p]

[*] Fix for crash on load game

[*] Fix for crewman remaining after bail out

[/list]

[h2]42-31367 Chow-Hound[/h2]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/920e3f10add009e75d993443c0733b0f46d233b6.jpg[/img]

By early August of 1944 the allies were pushing south of the beach head in Normandy. The allied plan relied on heavy bombers to soften the German lines. These missions were often considered 'Milk-Runs' by the crews, as they were usually unchallenged by German fighters. For the mission of August 8, 1944 the 91st would send three squadrons of B-17s to hit German positions that were confronting the Canadian First Army south of Caen. 

B17 42-31367  Chow-Hound had completed forty-eight missions with three crews. During this last mission disaster struck. The Chow-Hound was cut in half by a direct flak hit.  The Chow-Hound was lost with all hands. 

Due to the efforts of a French organisation ANSA, the location of the crash site was provided to the US department of defence in 2001, which performed an excavation of the site in 2004, recovering and repatriating the remains of three crew members who had been MIA for 60 years. A military funeral with full honors was held at Arlington Cemetery in 2006.

[b]Brave the deadly skies of occupied Europe![/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/b9cf358297bbb4a2d98ef4aa459264f8b2430413.png[/img]

notes.title: 1.0.17 Ain’t it Gruesome
notes.content:
This build contains user modifiable nose art and control changes

[h1]Features[/h1]
- Any PNG added to UserAssets/NoseArt/New can be added to your B17 as nose art. Nose art must be 512x512 or smaller. 
- Controller gamepad can be bound as buttons
- Controller Triggers can be bound as buttons

[h1]42-29863 - Ain't it Gruesome[/h1]
In 1943, Clark Gable, star of 'Gone With The Wind' was one of Hollywood's most famous actors. After the death of his wife in a plane crash in 1942 he enlisted in the Army Air Forces, joining the 8th Air Force. He flew as a gunner and cameraman on several missions.

On 12th August 1943, he was gunner in B17 #42-29863 'Ain't it Gruesome' in a raid over Germany. He had wedged himself behind the top turret gunner for a better view. He almost lost his life when a 20mm shell went through the flight deck, removing the heel of his shoe and missing his head by 30 cm.

The footage collected by Gable and his crew was used to produce 'Combat America', a documentary on B17's used to promote war bonds.

notes.title: Dev Blog Update: Controls
notes.content:
TLDR: Your controls may need a rebind after the next update. 

For the last few weeks we’ve been working on updating the way B17:The Mighty Eighth handles controls. This has been a top to bottom change involving configuration and game systems. The original game stored all data in a binary options file. Controller information is stored based on the order that windows presents the controllers to the game, which means that adding or removing controllers can mess up player’s bindings. Default controls were also stored this way, making it tricky to alter the game to add new bindings.

We’ve updated the default control bindings to be in a human readable standard JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) format, this will allow us greater flexibility to add new controls and fields. We’ve also updated the user’s individual control bindings to include the unique identifier of each control, meaning your bindings will stay consistent when adding or removing peripherals. This will also allow us to support a wider array of peripherals in future updates, or a more focused experience for players who play on Steam Deck or with game controllers.

We’ve added a migration for your existing bindings, from the old format to the new format. This should be seamless for most users, however a rebind of controls may be necessary.

Here at MicroProse we consider working on Mighty 8th Redux to be a labour of love. It serves as a real and direct link to our company’s history. Thank you for helping us bring this game to a new generation!

Brave the deadly skies!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/b9cf358297bbb4a2d98ef4aa459264f8b2430413.png[/img]

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/5b9f31f263d40dd4de8ae358fa7f2d9625aa86f0.jpg[/img][h2]Features[/h2]

[h2]Jersey Bounce Jr.[/h2]
It was radio operator Forrest Vostler's fourth mission in B-17 42-29664 'Jersey Bounce Jr' on a mission to Bremen. After the B-17 had bombed its target, it was damaged by Antiaircraft fire and forced out of formation, making it a target of opportunity for German fighters. 

The aircraft was hit by multiple 20mm cannon shells, two of which exploded in the radio compartment, severely damaging Vostler's legs, chest and face, including shrapnel in his eyes. 

The severely damaged aircraft limped most of the way home, with the crew jettisoning any extra weight they could. 

Despite both sets of injuries Vostler kept firing at the enemy, and then after the pilot announced they would have to ditch in the channel, although he could barely see and was barely conscious he managed to fumble around with the damaged radio enough to send a distress signal.

Due to Vostler's actions all crew survived. For his bravery he was awarded the congressional medal of honor.


Brave the deadly skies of occupied Europe!

notes.title: Update 1.0.14 "My Prayer"
notes.content:
[h1]Update 1.0.14 - My Prayer[/h1]

This patch contains an updated virtual cockpit with most dials and gauges implemented. Lights and switches will be added soon afterwards. It also contains optimisations for main memory and video memory, and fixes for controls.

[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] B17 Cockpit Dials & Gauges
[*] B17 Cockpit Camera Controls Updated
[*] Action View: HAT and Padlock controls
[*] Instrument View: F4-F8 keys to go directly to OG views. Arrow keys to cycle through views including new views.
[*] Window View: Mouse look and Instrument Snap control (defaults to Ctrl-P) to enable cockpit interaction mode. Useful for some hard to reach places from other views like the Prop Pitch levers.
[/list]

[h2]Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Memory optimisations, to prevent framerate issues for some users
[*] Main menu will no longer wrongly map to HOTAS throttle controllers
[*] Fix for crash to desktop when a crewman is unable to get a next viable position
[/list]

[h2]My Prayer[/h2]

42-5712 'My Prayer' was on a mission near Frankfurt when it was hit by three 20mm incendiary cannon rounds which exploded in the wing and under the pilots compartment, setting fire to the aircraft. The Bombardier and Navigator immediately bailed out. Due to smoke and flames the pilot lost control, but managed to recover from a slow spin at 6000 feet.  Co Pilot Roger Layn oversaw most of the other men bailing out, in some instances 'using force' to make sure the parachutes were properly adjusted,  however Earl Cherry, the engineer, was wounded and his parachute burnt.

Pilot James D. Judy decided to try to return home. He dropped to 100 feet and flew a zig-zag pattern over occupied territory while Cherry and Layn fought spot fires and fired at enemy fighters, burning out both waist guns. The pilot managed to fly back to England to crash land on grass at RAF Manston. All crewmen survived.

Brave the deadly skies of occupied Europe!

[h3][i]Microprose[/i][/h3]

notes.title: Update 1.0.13 - "Tondelayo"
notes.content:
Update 1.0.13 - Tondelayo

This patch contains major underlying changes to the damage system to alleviate frame rate issues when taking damage. A new olive skin has been added and the patch also contains a number of other fixes.

[h3]Features[/h3]
- Olive skin 
- There's been some deep changes to the way that damage changes skin textures, rewriting the system to work on hardware. This should alleviate frame drops when there is a lot of damage happening to multiple B17s
- Rationalisation of fighter attack waves

[h3]Fixes[/h3]
- There's a fix for sliding targets while looking through the Norden Bombsight
- There's been a fix for joysticks with throttle and rotational control to allow these to be bound

[b]Tondelayo[/b]
B17 42-29896, 'Tondelayo',  was named after a Hedy Lamarr movie. It was hit by multiple 20mm shells during a raid over Kassel, including several incendiary shells to the fuel tanks, but failed to ignite. When the shells were later analysed they were all found to be empty, except for one, which had a carefully rolled piece of paper, with a note written in Czech by a laborer forced to work for the Nazis 'This is all we can do for you now'

Ensure you follow the game for updates on the roadmap and patch notes.

Microprose

notes.title: DEV BLOG #8 - Update 1.0.12 - Memphis Belle
notes.content:
[b][h2]Update 1.0.12 - Memphis Belle[/h2][/b]

B-17 F 41-24485 'Memphis Belle' was named after pilot Robert K. Morgan's sweetheart, Margaret Polk, who lived in Memphis Tennessee. It was one of the first B17's to complete 25 combat missions, after which it was returned to the United States to help sell war bonds. It inspired two films, a 1944 documentary, and a 1990 feature film. It was restored in 2005 and is on display at the National Museum of the United States Air Force in Dayton, Ohio

[b][h2]Watch The New Update Showcase Video[/h2][/b]

[previewyoutube=ccm0MwyFdys;full][/previewyoutube]

[b][h2]New Features[/h2][/b]
New B-17
We’ve modelled a brand new B-17, with the top level of detail coming in at just over 50,000 polygons. 

To achieve this, we had to make numerous behind-the-scenes improvements including reconstructing the original model and rig from the compiled version, and then upgrading the import/export tools and pipeline by an order of magnitude.

The enhanced B-17 model contains a whole host of new and upgraded features, including:
[b]Cheyenne Tail Turret[/b]
Just like the 8th Air Force, we’ve upgraded our G model B-17 with a Cheyenne tail turret for better visibility and increased effectiveness!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/bda923472cf05ff26ede9496a640de1117259a44.jpg[/img]

[b]Upgraded Texture Damage[/b]
We’ve upgraded the dynamic texture damage system to improve performance and visual impact. The fuselage damage now supports transparency so that you can see into the B-17 through the holes, and we’ve added dynamic texture damage to glass surfaces as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/f081f0d3d801a8ab7c6f446fb502131afb3e67e2.jpg[/img]

[b]Physical Damage[/b]
In addition to upgrading the dynamic texture damage, the B-17 can now display the results of catastrophic damage using physically modelled damage components. These represent sheared off wingtips, tailplanes and holes punched through the airframe - ratcheting up the tension of nursing home a wounded aircraft!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/58a901d538cb3fba46035db726279b101cc7a91f.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/49f12a60ac4f7d7d9e7400f407b3b125745701a3.jpg[/img]

[b]Historical Liveries[/b]
We’ve added new 4K textures with unique markings for each bomb group. Depending on the mission start date, either olive drab or natural metal finish (NMF) skins will be used (with March 1944 as the changeover date)

[b]Serial Numbers[/b]
Each B17 will now display their unique serial number on their vertical stabilizer (tail fin).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/041f673b8c40912388112afdabfb2b86f09bfd27.jpg[/img]

[b]Dynamic Crew[/b]
The crew will now turn on and off on the exterior model as they assume or leave their positions. 

As an added easter egg, we’ve used the original high-definition (at the time) character models from the compartment views of the original B-17 as our crew on the new plane’s exterior view.

[b]Rendering Improvements[/b]
We’ve also added new pixel shader functionality to the engine, improving the specular highlights on the aircraft and paving the way for normal mapping in a future release.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/48e7d8f06d8200414af7e8063842b59ded4359f4.jpg[/img]

[b]Optimized Graphics Settings[/b]
We’ve adjusted the graphics settings to allow users with older graphics cards to continue to experience the game. 

PLEASE NOTE: The default settings are currently set to the BALANCED setting. Users with modern graphics cards should set them to DETAIL to experience the new updates in all their splendour.

[b]Damage Modelling[/b]
[list]
[*]This controls the dynamic texture damage system (includes the nose art and tailplane serial number features as well). 
[*]The default setting is currently BALANCED. There is currently no difference between BALANCED and DETAIL.
[*]Setting it to SPEED will reduce VRAM usage by disabling texture damage modelling entirely. 
[/list]

[b]General Quality[/b]
[list]
[*]This controls texture size in game. 
[*]The default setting of BALANCED offers HD (1080p) textures. 
[*]The DETAIL setting offers the full 4K textures.
[*]Setting it to SPEED offers the lowest quality, minimum VRAM usage (for users with older video cards).
[/list]

Thank you for your continuing support, enthusiasm and feedback as we continue our journey with B-17 Redux.  Good luck out there and we’ll see you in the air!

notes.title: B-17 THE MIGHTY 8TH REDUX - DEV BLOG #7
notes.content:
Greetings Folks,
We’ve been working hard for the last few months to deliver the fully updated HD ‘4k’ version of our latest B-17 aircraft model. It’s been quite the journey, with a lot of twists and turns along the way.

The new model tops out at 50k polygons, compared to the original’s 2.5k, which ironically is now the polygon count for the lowest level of detail. We even use the original model for the OG crew member in the HD B-17, so you can see each crew member in detail and inside the aircraft. 

We felt today was a great opportunity to share more specific details about the work accomplished already, and how that translates into the features you’ll see in our next game update.

[previewyoutube=R52mut8V-qM;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Tech Improvements[/h3]

-[b]Scene Groups Increased from 64 to 128[/b]
[list]
[*] Allows for improved damage meshes
[/list]
-[b]Updated “Skin” Damage System[/b] (Bullets, Smoke, Oil, Decals)
[list]
[*] The original game used many textures that were much smaller in size  (64x64, 128x128), whereas the new model uses improved 4k textures. The skin damage system has also been updated for performance and memory efficiency.
[/list]
-[b]Multiple Livery Support [/b]
[list]
[*] B-17 textures and material properties can now change by bomb group.
[/list]
-[b]Improved Performance -  MAX Exporte / , OMF CLI [/b]
[list]
[*] HD B-17 model scene (including all LODs and Damage) is 300k triangles vs 10k in the original game. Export process is now improved by an order of magnitude.
[*] MAX exporter was upgraded to do a better job of determining face transparency. Originally labeled a face as transparent if the material texture had any transparency on it. 
[/list]
-[b]Bone nodes added to Skin:[/b]
[list]
[*] Originally, the skin exporter ignored bones, which given the complexity of the new B-17 caused a bunch of problems. So we’ve added support to the skin for bones, allowing the skeleton to drive the scene graph.
[/list]
-[b]New ‘Per-Pixel’ Specular Shader[/b]
[list]
[*] OG had per-face specular, a new shader has been implemented for per-pixel specular for better visual impact.
[/list]

[h3]Art Improvements[/h3]

-[b]New HD B-17 Model @  50k+ polygons [/b]

-[b]New Physical Damage Components:[/b]
[list]
[*]Actual panels modeled with flak and bullet damage that will augment the dynamic texture damage system, increasing immersion and emotional investment/engagement
[/list]
-[b]Randomized bullet-hole size/shape on dynamic damage[/b]

-[b]4k textures - NMF, Olive, per group[/b]

-[b]Specular Restored[/b]

-[b]Crew able to turn on/off in external model as they take/leave positions[/b]

-[b]Reconstructed source data from compiled models[/b] - had to rebuild the source data (models, rigs, textures) from the game data as the originals were all lost to time

-[b]New Pipeline improvements[/b] - import, extraction, packer - this will help all future development updates.

-[b]Texture damage added to glass, as well as fuselage[/b]

-[b]Fuselage texture damage now supports transparency, so we now see inside and through bullet holes[/b]

[h3]STILL TO COME |  IN-DEVELOPMENT[/h3]

-[b]Virtual Cockpit[/b] [More details and updates on this are planned, so rest assured!]

[h3]Screenshots[/h3]
It's come a long way.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/da4cfe6d5778d92ce7764f1a8d58ad79ad0021d5.jpg[/img]

Bullet holes are generated using a secondary texture and Barycentric transformations from world space positions into texture space. The texel density governs the size of the holes, which are too small here:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/8c316f17549f7fccf053116295f080576641d11e.png[/img]

What does the texel density look like?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/118aad433f12a4a5966bb871f8eed2da6c45c1ac.png[/img]

notes.title: Update 1.0.11 - Susan Ruth
notes.content:
This patch contains major fighter and AI changes

[h2]Major Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fix for aircraft targeting overflow causing bullets not to impact fighters after a while
[*] Chin, Cheek, Ball, Left Waist and Right waist guns now fire and hit targets
[/list]

[h2]Minor Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Damage is more sensibly applied to physics components, damage to control surfaces will now effect control
[*] When an aircraft is hit with bullets, we mark is as damaged by bullets so that when/if it crashes into the ground we'll count it as shot down instead of 'accidental'
[*] Fix for UV crawling on terrain
[*] Binding a joystick axis no longer blocks keys
[*] Fix for time skip failing due to bombardier after bombing target
[*] Windows Icon
[/list]
[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] Different enemy fighter squadrons now have tuneable skill levels. The skill level of enemy fighters at the moment random on Mission levels, but will steadily ramp up in 'Attack of the Axis'
[*] All B17 Gunners are now hitting with significantly more accuracy 
[/list]

B17 42-31499 'Susan Ruth' was one of 20 B17s from the 306th bombardment group to bomb the Frankfurt rail yards on 8th February 1944. It was damaged by flak over the target, but remained flyable, however the bomber was targeted by two German fighters over France, killing the radio operator and the ball turret gunner, and forcing the rest of the crew to bail out of the mortally wounded aircraft.

Scattered over the countryside, 5 of the surviving crew managed to evade capture for a while with the help of Belgian and French resistance, but 3 were eventually captured and executed by Nazi partisans. Too injured to make the arduous journey over the Pyrenees to Spain and allied Gibraltar, the pilot, Howard J Snyder, joined the 'The Maquis', a local resistance group, and continued to fight the Nazi regime from the ground until liberated by US troops months later.

Boy oh boy, second patch in as many days. This one fixes a very serious CTD mid-mission and tweaks the new time bar.

[*] No longer able to change speed while paused
[*] Icon bar help no longer shows if icons are invisible
[/list]


B-17 serial 42-32076 was accepted into service in January 1944 arriving in Great Britain on the 2nd of March. It was flown from RAF Bassingbourn by the 401st bombardment squadron of the 91st bombardment group. Dubbed 'Shoo Shoo Baby' by its crew after a popular song by the Andrews Sisters, it flew 24 successful missions, before mechanical problems deep in enemy territory forced the crew to land the Aircraft in neutral Sweden where it was interned. A deal was struck between the US and Sweden to gift several B17's to Sweden for civilian purposes including the (renamed) 'Shoo Shoo Shoo Baby', in return for repatriation of air crew. 

Shoo Shoo Shoo Baby is one of a handful of surviving B17's today.

notes.title: Update 1.0.7 - Winged Victory
notes.content:
This patch fixes several AI issues and includes some Quick Mission and Front End enhancements.

[b]Bomber Formation AI[/b]
[*] Catastrophic collisions should be significantly reduced when formations are turning
[*] Bombers will leave formation if they cannot maintain cruise speed

Note: Flak damage severely impacts the aircraft control surfaces, which impacts the bombers' ability to maintain formation positioning currently. We're aware of this and are continuing to work on improvements to this.

[b]Fighter Attack AI[/b]
[*] Fighter->B17 collisions should be significantly reduced
[*] Fighter AI will avoid bomber formation airspace
[*] Fighters will abort and head home after 4 passes (instead of 15 minutes), absent damage, fuel low, out of ammo
[*] When breaking off an attack, fighters will maintain break off posture until clear of the target
[*] When intercepting the target, fighters will abort if they get too close if that have failed to begin Attacking
[*] Gunners will only announce fighters if the fighter is directly attacking

[b]Attack of the Axis[/b]
[*] More squadrons, more fighters
[*] Attack wave squadrons are staggered

[b]Front End[/b]
[*] Controls can be reset with right click (on the control window on the right)
[*] Text windows in the front end will page up/down with mouse wheel

Please keep the feedback coming and follow the game on social and on the major gaming platforms for the latest updates.

notes.title: Update 1.0.1
notes.content:
[h1]Update Notes 1.0.1[/h1]

Thanks for taking the time to give us your feedback and report any issues you have spotted. Today we are bringing you the first patch which includes updates to elements within the game that have been spotted by our test pilots.


[h2]Training Missions[/h2]
[list]
[*] Manual control locks will no longer occur during the “Training #1: Pilot Checkout” mission
[*] Legacy takeoff training mission has been re-added

[h2]Role Adjustments[/h2]

[list]
[*] Radio Operator no longer has a window or action view
[*] Legacy issue: Radio operator is now able to check the weather at the decision point not just the initial point

[*] Legacy issue: Radio operator is now able to change to an alternative target at the decision point, not just the initial point

[*] Co-Pilot action view now operates the same as the pilot action view

notes.title: B-17 The Mighty 8th Redux Dev Blog #2
notes.content:
Welcome aboard followers, new and old.

In this Dev Blog, we are going to answer some of your questions and show some more progress on the game. If you’ve been hanging out for some gunner stations, this one is for you. 

[h2]Comparison Shots the Top Gunner[/h2]

Today we can share the progress the team has made on the Top Gunner position. Here we can show you the comparison shot from the gunner’s perspective – do note that the aircraft you see in the distance has yet to be replaced with the new model. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/407c0d72c28d6c4e8acbb0f973b2e7b69fba2bbb.jpg[/img]
[i]Top Gunner - old model[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/3de3b170a84c0da8f204e34cea0872b953c86afc.jpg[/img]
[i]Top Gunner - new model[/i]

Our artists are also happy to share with you some of their modeling work on the Top Turret. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/5988e29218e9aeb0def7928795e24e3d6b889509.jpg[/img]
[i]Top Gunner - model[/i]

[h2]The Ball Turret[/h2]

One of the scariest seats on the B-17 is currently being brought into Redux. We are happy to share the progress on this. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/877d551805e6190beac09c9532d70962afcc2cae.jpg[/img]

[i]Ball Turret model[/i]

Here is how that currently looks in-game. Do bear in mind that what you see outside the aircraft is not final.  As the aircraft exteriors and terrain is updated, we will share that progress with you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/32806a808e7184a46fc6f6d44ac94c8a1924e334.jpg[/img]

[i]Ball Turret in-game[/i]

[h2]Continued Progress on the Nose[/h2]

One of the areas we have continued to focus on is the navigator’s table, where we have incorporated a new map. You will notice a few other changes as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/8f91914fbb894ada9cdfd59b55cfe0bbb90ea148.jpg[/img]
[i]Navigator progress[/i]

For fans of navigation, we are also happy to share some maps from our collection that would have been used by crews during WW2. The first map is Lubeck, followed by Bolzano and Bordeaux.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/ff9666ec735e943a0415099a3fd7572f953bb5fb.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/007a4c314b6dbed221a1b558df22c863afc07a93.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43121699/ff9666ec735e943a0415099a3fd7572f953bb5fb.jpg[/img]

[i]Navigator map[/i]

[h2]Questions from Discord[/h2]

Our community manager has been gathering questions from our followers on Discord (link) and other social locations.

We will answer a few of these questions with each post. Keep the questions coming.

[b]Are we able to fly the fighters as well like in the original? And if so, are new German fighters planned like the Bf-110 and many more? Are we able to fly the fighters as well like in the original? And if so, are new German fighters planned like the Bf-110 and many more?
[/b]

We are working to bring the fighter aircraft into the Redux. Precisely how many and what models will be in the initial Early Access release will be announced closer to the release. There are currently not any plans for additional aircraft, but that’s a good suggestion. 

[b]Will there be more mechanical failures will the crew have more tasks like the radio operator and navigator?[/b]

Currently, there are no additional failures being considered, but this is another great suggestion. I think we might prod the team working on “[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1752530/B17_Flying_Fortress_The_Bloody_100th/]The Bloody 100th[/url]” to increase the emergencies a player can face though.

[b]How will the movement system work? Will it be like the original TME with only clicking through the positions or are we able to walk through the B-17 in first-person?[/b]

We are being true to the original game in this respect, so you won’t be able to move through the B17 in first-person view. However, this will be possible in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1325580/The_Mighty_Eighth_VR/]The Mighty 8th VR[/url]. 

[h2]Comic Pages Delayed[/h2]

We wanted to hold off on sending through this update until we were 100% happy with the next pages of the comic, but you can look forward to those in an interim post in the coming weeks.

[h2]Thanks for your support so far...[/h2]

Thanks for joining us for the latest update, I look forward to updating you again soon.  Keep those questions coming.
